facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old woman presented for evaluation of her worsening skin condition
The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs were sparse and less than 5 mm long
her scalp hairs were coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy: Showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)

concepts.why: The patient's widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale and psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy are characteristic of Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.
The patient's erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale and psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy are consistent with Psoriasis.
The patient's sparse eyebrow hairs, coarse and brittle scalp hairs, and trichography showing nodal swelling are suggestive of Alopecia Areata.
The patient's erythematous plaques and spongiosis on skin biopsy could also be seen in Eczema.
The patient's erythematous plaques and psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy could also be consistent with Seborrheic Dermatitis.

rationales.F03: The presence of widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale is highly suggestive of Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris and Psoriasis.
rationales.F04: Sparse eyebrow hairs are a characteristic feature of Alopecia Areata.
rationales.F05: Coarse and brittle scalp hairs can be seen in Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris and Alopecia Areata.
rationales.F06: Psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy is highly indicative of Psoriasis.
rationales.F07: Nodal swelling and invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end on trichography can be seen in Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris and Alopecia Areata.

frontier_selector.rationale: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris best explains the combination of widespread skin involvement, characteristic plaques, and hair findings, with no strong contradictions.
